statement: Build a single-file website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru where patients can request visits, find emergency information, read doctor profiles and a health blog, and use the whole site in English, Kannada and Hindi.
audience: Patients and their families in Bengaluru, reading English, Kannada or Hindi, many on phones and some in an urgent situation.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Plain, calm wording a non-specialist can follow; emergency information is the most prominent content on every page.
Readable and usable on phones and desktops, with keyboard-reachable controls and readable contrast.
Kannada text is in Kannada script and Hindi text is in Devanagari script, with no machine-looking mixed or untranslated sentences.
No invented medical facts: every emergency number, doctor name, qualification and specialty not given in the brief appears as a clearly marked placeholder.
rules: Booking is a request form, not live slot booking. The site promises that staff confirm by phone or WhatsApp and never implies instant confirmation.
Emergency numbers, doctor names, qualifications and specialties are shipped as clearly marked placeholders and listed as open inputs.
The site must not be published as live until the placeholder medical facts are confirmed, because wrong emergency information is a patient-safety risk.
Every page, the blog included, is translated into Kannada and Hindi and flagged as awaiting native-speaker review.
Anything needing facts or an outside source is a marked placeholder on the site, not a guess.
done_when: The site is one HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline or loaded from a CDN, needing no build step.
The file contains navigable sections for Home, Book a Visit, Emergency, Doctors and Health Blog, all reachable from a navigation menu.

The Book a Visit section has a request form with fields for patient name, phone number, preferred date, department or doctor, and reason for visit, and visible text saying staff will confirm by phone or WhatsApp.
The form text makes no claim of instant or automatic confirmation, and the file has no live slot picker or backend call.
Emergency information is visible from every view, either in the header or a persistent banner, and includes an emergency number shown as a marked placeholder.
The Doctors section has several profile cards, each with name, specialty and qualifications, every one shown as a marked placeholder.
The Health Blog section lists posts, and at least one post opens or expands to its full text.
A language switch offers English, Kannada and Hindi, and choosing one changes the text of every section, the booking form labels and every blog post, with the page language attribute updated.
Each language view has complete translations: no section, form label, button or blog post is left in English in the Kannada or Hindi view, apart from proper names and marked placeholders.
Every placeholder carries the same visible 'to be confirmed' marking in all three languages, and the site shows a visible list of all placeholders still open.
The site shows a visible notice that the Kannada and Hindi text is awaiting native-speaker review, and a visible notice that placeholder medical facts are not final.
The file includes a mobile viewport setting and a layout that adapts to narrow screens, so the menu, form and emergency information stay usable.
open_inputs: Real emergency phone numbers and any emergency-department details (placeholder shown on site).
Real doctor names, qualifications and specialties (placeholders shown on site).
Hospital departments or services offered, for the booking form choices.
The phone number and WhatsApp number staff use to confirm booking requests.
Hospital address, general contact details and opening hours.
Native-speaker review of the Kannada and Hindi text.
Medical accuracy of the health blog posts, which are drafted by us.
